Blocks.Text: In order to ensure that integrations deliver an optimal user experience, all Display Services partner integrations are reviewed prior to launch. This document describes the criteria we use to evaluate integrations to ensure best practices to the external application's context have been implemented that are relevant.
During certification, solutions migrating to Display 2.1 will be reviewed to ensure that the Authentication Requirements are met. This includes:

Implementation of the provisioning API as described in the requirements documentation.
Implementation of Sales Access Tokens
Storage of Access Tokens for subsequent usage
Domain allow list defined for on child applications
Following of Display 2.1 best practices, including adoption of programmatic refresh tokens and using all tokens for the duration of their TTL.
The following use cases/functionality will need to be demoed during certification:

Rows.Text: Customer UX for enabling of the integration and implement of Provisioning API
Enabling integration incorporates provisioning API either overtly or transparently to administrators.
Customer sign in experience to iframe
User can sign in using SAT flow, best practices followed.
Following removing grant from permitted services, users can re-login without issue.

Blocks.Text: In order to achieve the best possible adoption for your integration, we recommend users get opted-in to Sales Navigator integration by default. We've ranked a range of options, from most to least recommended below:

Opt organizations/accounts in by default, and enable users/admins to disable (preferred)
Opt users in by default, enable users to disable
Allow entire accounts/organizations to opt-in
Allow individual users to opt-in

We find that it is helpful in most cases to allow users to disable the integration if it is not wanted. One of the things we look for during integration reviews is that the onboarding flow is optimal for the application context.

Matching is a core part of the experience for users of the Display Services. All users will interact with the matching flow, and it is important that the integration is designed to take full advantage of the persistence offered by the iframe, as described in our matching documentation. When evaluating matching implementations, we look for:

Using a unique external identifier in the crmRecordId field for the entity (lead or account) you are trying to load in the iframe.
If a unique ID is not available, using a hashing function to generate a consistent value for the entity.
Sending crmSourceType in every request--without it persistence does not work.
If your implementation uses Sales Access Tokens, we will validate that your implementation meets the following requirements:

Access tokens are never sent to clients
Access tokens are encrypted at rest
We will also review the process you use to determine expired Sales Access Tokens and refresh them to ensure optimal user experience.

Finally, we also validate that a valid client ID is passed to us in the apiKey parameter in every request, and that the developer application has configured https://www.linkedin.com as a Valid JS Domain on developer.linkedin.com. This enables the Sign In button to be shown for users with no active session.
